title: When Interpretability Meets Generalization: Delta-GAM for Robust Extrapolation in Out-of-Distribution Settings

problem.claim: Out-of-distribution extrapolation is challenging when test feature values extend beyond the training range.

gap.claim: Existing solutions often sacrifice interpretability, limiting applicability in high-stakes settings.

contributions.claim: Delta-GAM jointly learns feature-target relationships and functional adaptations for extrapolation beyond the training distribution.
Smooth GAM shape functions induce an approximately low-rank structure that enables efficient decomposition through a specialized neural network.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world data report superior performance in out-of-distribution extrapolation while preserving interpretability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real-world data demonstrate superior performance in out-of-distribution extrapolation tasks.
The reported method preserves model interpretability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Out-of-distribution extrapolation beyond the training feature range poses significant machine-learning challenges.
Existing approaches may trade away interpretability, creating limitations for high-stakes applications.
Delta-GAM is introduced as an interpretable GAM that learns both feature-target relationships and extrapolation adaptations.
The method uses an approximately low-rank interaction structure induced by smooth GAM shape functions for efficient decomposition.
Synthetic and real-world experiments report superior extrapolation performance while retaining interpretability.

source_observation.claim: The method jointly models ordinary feature-target relationships and adaptations associated with distributional offsets.

interpretation.claim: Robust extrapolation may benefit from explicitly representing how relationships change outside the observed training range.

application.claim: For interpretable models deployed under distribution shift, consider separating baseline relationships from shift-related functional adaptations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers to settings beyond the reported experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not detail the specialized neural network or the theoretical assumptions and guarantees.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
